title: Friction atelier: mini lab notes and probe backlog
body:
Summary:
Quick capture from the "atelier" session with frontline CS + one SRE + one ENG PM. Goal: turn frequent, low-effort customer asks about inference friction into a set of tiny, testable probes (<= 2 dev-days each). This doc collects the synthesized asks, suggested probe designs, and rough prioritization with engineering cost signals.

Context / why now:
- Several customers (two fintech, one mid-market SaaS, one design tool startup) reported repeated latency/consistency pain when switching model variants during spikes.
- Field notes point to 3 recurring triggers: cold KV-cache after rollouts, routing to incompatible quantized variants, and surprise burst throttling on shared pools.
- Not a single large outage; more a steady churn of support tickets and usage drop-offs. We want low-friction fixes that reduce repeats and give CS tactical wins.

Representative customer quotes (anonymized):
- "Every time we flip a model during nightly rollouts our tail latency doubles for a few minutes — users hang and retry." (fintech-customer)
- "We saw a single request route to a cheaper quantized host and the output changed subtly; model drift/regression worries us more than raw latency." (enterprise-saas)
- "Our dev team needs a small knob to 'prefer warm cache' for the first X minutes after deploys." (design-tool-startup)

Key themes (synth):
1) Warm-cache UX: customers want explicit, simple controls to avoid cold-KV spikes after deploys or during scaling events.
2) Fallback transparency: when we fallback to cheaper/quantized variants, teams want signals and optional auto-rollback triggers tied to evals.
3) Burst protection: predictable degradation (graceful tails) is preferred to opaque throttling + request drops.
4) Observability gaps: token-level cost + per-request variant metadata is not always surfaced to customers' dashboards.

Micro-probes (<= 2 dev-days, ranked):
A. "deploy-warm-window" flag (priority: high) — small API toggle to mark a model rollout window (e.g., 10m) where requests preferentially route to instances with warmed KV caches or where we prioritize warm-host scheduling. Minimal infra change: routing policy check + transient tag. Success signal: 30% fewer tail-latency spikes in next 72h for pilot client. Linked: JIRA-5247.
B. "fallback-reporting" shim (priority: medium-high) — emit a per-request header + dashboard row when request used a fallback variant (quantized/cheaper). Surface counts in Console and send optional webhook to customer's telemetry. Success: pilot customer stops filing 'unknown fallback' tickets.
C. "graceful-burst-queue" experiment (priority: medium) — short-lived elastic queue that smooths bursts and returns an estimated wait-time header instead of immediate throttle. Requires small SRE work + config. Success: reduce error-rate on spike windows by 40% in experiment.
D. Quick KV-cache inspector CLI (priority: low) — internal tool for CS to ask 'is my prefix cached?': shows hit-rate for given customer keys. Fast win for debug calls.

Suggested quick patches & trade-offs (notes):
- Warm-window routing is cheap but increases cost slightly (more warm-host usage). Trade vs retention: acceptable for high-churn customers.
- Fallback-reporting has low risk but may surface a lot of noisy signals; we should include a sampling toggle.
- Graceful-queue adds latency for some users; document UX expectations and provide a toggle for customers who prefer immediate failure.

Metrics to instrument (for pilots):
- Per-customer 95th/99th latency before/after deploy for 72h windows.
- Count of fallback events per-customer per-hour + fraction leading to customer complaint.
- KV-cache warm-hit ratio on host pools after rollout.
- Customer retention delta (short-term) for pilot cohort.

Prototype plan & owners:
- Evelyn (CS) will own pilot coordination + write customer-facing runbook.
- Samir (SRE) to spike routing flag mechanics and impact on scheduler (estimate: 1.5d).
- Asha (ENG PM) to scope Console surface for fallback-reporting (estimate: 2d).
- Miguel (SWE) to build KV-cache inspector (0.5d).

Open questions / unknowns (notes for engineering):
- How do we ensure warm-host selection doesn't starve low-traffic customers? (scheduling fairness)
- Can we tie fallback reporting to automated eval checks so we only alert when a quality regression is detected? (costly but high-value)
- Is there a simple heuristic for 'prefer warm cache' that plays well with autoscaling?

Customer pilot list (candidates):
- Fintech A (high sensitivity to tail latency; willing to be first pilot)
- DesignTool B (small team; wants CLI debug tools)
- Enterprise SaaS C (concerned about regressions; wants fallback transparency)

Next steps (short):
- T+2 days: Samir delivers routing-flag PoC and runbook for pilot.
- T+4 days: Miguel pushes KV-inspector alpha to CS sandbox.
- T+7 days: Asha wires basic fallback-reporting telemetry to a staging Console view.
- Schedule three 45m pilot onboarding sessions (CS + customer engineers).

Notes-to-self / friction log snippets:
- Keep probes small; our primary goal is to lower ticket volume by 30% on these themes.
- Flag naming: use stable semantics ("prefer-warm-window") so customers can read it in audits.
- Prepare templated explanation for customers about cost trade-offs and expected improvements.

Appendix: quick references
- Prior support threads: slack:#cs-runtime-ops-thread-2024-10-07 -> includes raw logs attached.
- Related Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/FRICTION-atelier-2024 (design sketches + meeting notes)
- Jira: JIRA-5247 (routing warm-window), JIRA-5319 (fallback reporting backlog)

End of notes.

-- Evelyn
(working draft; will iterate after spike results)
